name: AlJannat Adeola Uthman
feedback: D1: your catalogue is well disciplined on method, you state you only used the source comments as a map and proved behaviour from the artefacts, and you correctly nailed the SQL injection in 01-legacy-admin-login.php lines 64-67 (A03/CWE-89) and the unsalted MD5 at line 66 (A02/CWE-916) with quoted lines, plus XXE in 04-import-xxe.xml (A05/CWE-611) and the stored XSS cookie beacon to 185.220.101.9:8443 (CWE-79). Where you lost ground is coverage. You catalogued only about five of the ten findings, and you omitted the entire JWT cluster (alg:none accepted A07/CWE-347, hardcoded secret sankofa-legacy-admin-2019 A02/CWE-798, no token expiry A07/CWE-613) and the access-control set (path traversal A01/CWE-22, open redirect ?next= A01/CWE-601, cookie missing Secure/SameSite A05/CWE-614), so the access-control row scored zero in D1 even though you used path traversal later in D2. Your decoy work is excellent and is the single best part of D1, you named the hash_equals branch as the safe construct and proved it constant-time at the mechanism level, which is exactly right, but note that alg:none is a real live vulnerability you missed, not part of the safe construct. D2: the chain is mostly in order and reconciled to capture lines with verbatim PoCs carrying the PHPSESSID and source IP, which is strong, but you dropped the open redirect hop at 02:21:13 and your SQLi CVSS vector is wrong, you scored AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H at 9.8 when the bypass does not hit availability, so the correct vector is A:N giving roughly 9.1, and one of your other vectors was left truncated with a blank availability metric. Your naira impact is good, 312 customers with a stated balance range and the BoltCash six-week launch tie-in earns most of that row. D3: the executive summary is genuinely jargon-free and lands on customers and naira, the threat model is concrete, the disproved decoy is restated correctly, and your two detection stopgaps name exact endpoints, regex fields and false-positive rates, which is exactly what was asked. The weak point is the remediation table, you supplied effort estimates but your ordering rationale is risk reduction and chain position rather than effort-to-risk, which caps that row, and the findings list inherits the same coverage gap as D1. D4: a clean, own-voice ethics answer that covers all four prompts, cites ISC2 Canon I and Canon II by number and load-bearing, and anchors to your own SQLi finding and the 312 records. You named the NDPA 2023 NDPC notification duty and tied it to the 312 customers but you did not cite the sections, so add section 40 (notify the NDPC within 72 hours) and section 41 (notify data subjects on high risk) to make it load-bearing. No fabrication was present, your impact figures trace to the exfil sample and your decoy verdict is sound. I looked for a way to round the finding coverage higher and the catalogue simply does not support it, you need the missing five findings with quoted lines to move the D1 and D3 rows up. The single most important fix is to catalogue all ten findings with a quoted evidence line and correct OWASP plus CWE for each, especially the JWT alg:none and hardcoded secret you missed entirely.
